weekly_recap.previous_weekend: Josh Davis edged John Schauder 118.52 to 113.22, a gap of just 5.30 points that lands as the 7th smallest margin of victory in league history — the tightest game of the week. Amon-Ra St. Brown erupted for 28.5 points for Schauder, but Jerry Jeudy's putrid 5.0 points in the final game sealed the collapse before Schauder could even reach for the antacids. Meanwhile Davis, the reigning King of The Crawfish, rode Keenan Allen's monstrous 37.0-point outing like a lawn chair floating on a cooler of Coors, even as Derrick Henry did his best impression of a parked car, managing only 2.5 points. Schauder remains the league's eternal bridesmaid — good rosters, brutal schedules, and somehow always left holding the bouquet instead of the trophy, and tonight was no exception. Josh, meanwhile, gets to keep hosing down the crawfish boiler with another round of victory beer, crown still firmly attached.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: Billed as a genuine top-6 showdown, this one turned into target practice — Erik Servinsky rolled 135.06 to Carl Bruce's 102.58, a 32.48-point beatdown that closes their all-time series at 1-0 in Erik's favor. Dak Prescott torched everybody for 39.86 points, while Carl's Stefon Diggs limped home with a putrid 4.9 to help slam the door as the last game of the week wrapped. Carl, sitting on a modest 50.0 career winning percentage, now has to explain this one to nobody, because Erik — who complains about every trade like it's a personal insult — surely won't let him forget it anyway. Rough Sunday, rougher Monday morning.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week: Blacktop Bursitis rolls in as the 1st ranked squad in the league at 8-2, and Greg Wigton looks great doing it, because apparently the man was contractually obligated to remind everyone he's "really really good looking" while dropping 122.2 points a game this season on the rest of you. Jay Nelson's Combine Conquistadors sit ranked 2nd at 7-3, averaging 114.5 points a game, which is respectable until you remember he's also the trusted commissioner — the guy holding the keys to the league's integrity while quietly getting outscored on the field. Both schedules have graded out close enough that nobody gets to cry about strength of schedule here. This is the first-ever meeting between these two, so the head-to-head ledger starts at zero-zero today. Somebody's undefeated bragging rights or commissioner credibility takes a hit in the standings — pick your poison, gentlemen, the podium only fits one pretty face.
